identity.name: Potassium ascorbate
identity.chemical_class: Ascorbate salt (potassium salt of L-ascorbic acid)

function.mechanism: Acts as a reducing antioxidant (ascorbate), helping limit oxidative reactions in food matrices.
common_food_categories: Historically antioxidant uses in processed foods
Applications analogous to other ascorbate salts

adi.basis: No E303-specific EFSA ADI identified; EFSA 2015 re-evaluation for related ascorbates E300-E302 reported no need for a numerical ADI.

efsa.key_finding: Accessible EFSA opinion located for E300-E302 (2015) concluded no safety concern at reported uses and no genotoxicity concern; no dedicated E303 EFSA opinion was identified in this search.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR Part 182 (no explicit potassium ascorbate entry in current text); related ascorbate entries: 21 CFR 182.3189 and 21 CFR 182.3731

adi.basis: ADI NOT SPECIFIED (group ADI for ascorbic acid and its sodium, potassium and calcium salts).

notable_bans: JECFA database comment (2015): provisions for potassium ascorbate withdrawn at CCFA47.

concerns.summary: Direct modern food-additive toxicology evidence specific to potassium ascorbate is sparse; PubMed search for potassium ascorbate with toxicity/safety terms returned no items.
key_references: PubMed toxicity/safety query for potassium ascorbate

concerns.summary: High total/supplemental vitamin C intake has been associated with increased incident kidney stone risk in men (not specific to typical additive-level exposure).

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA group ADI not specified for ascorbic acid and sodium/potassium/calcium salts.
EFSA related ascorbate assessment (E300-E302) reported no safety concern and no genotoxicity concern at reported uses.

populations: Children/toddlers may have higher relative exposure to related ascorbate additives
adi_exceedance.notes: Formal ADI exceedance framing is limited because JECFA group ADI is not specified and EFSA related assessment did not set a numerical ADI.

risk_assessment.rationale: Related ascorbate toxicology is broadly reassuring (JECFA group ADI not specified; EFSA related assessment no safety concern), but E303-specific modern data and explicit CFR listing are limited.
key_factors: JECFA ADI not specified group finding
Sparse direct potassium ascorbate safety literature
No explicit current Title 21 CFR listing for potassium ascorbate
